messages.subject: NA formatting trouble in Occu
parts:
Hi,

I'm scared to post on here, especially such a basic question, but I'm stuck on a troublesome formatting issue with my survey covariates in Occu. I swear this should be an easy fix, but I'm not sure what else to try. If anyone would be willing to take a look with me I would sincerely appreciate it.

For the site covariates, my data set has 6 covariates and occu() has no problem
creating models from these:
o.elevation.effort<-occu(~1 ~elevation+avg.effort,pm.ss.std)
> o.elevation.effort

Call:
occu(formula = ~1 ~ elevation + avg.effort, data = pm.ss.std)

Occupancy:
            Estimate    SE      z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)  -0.3314 0.213 -1.554  0.1202
elevation    -0.0352 0.211 -0.167  0.8672
avg.effort    0.5839 0.231  2.526  0.0115

Detection:
 Estimate    SE    z  P(>|z|)
      1.8 0.228 7.88 3.17e-15

AIC: 272.2521

However, when I try to incorporate the survey/observation-specific covariates to model detection, the obsCovs cause R to become unhappy. For example, I get the following errors:


 p.julian<-occu(~julian ~1,pm.ss.std)
Warning message:
Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.

p.julian.obsvr<-occu(~julian+obsvr ~1,pm.ss.std)
Warning message:
Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.

> fitlist<-fitList(p.julian, p.julian.obsvr)
Warning messages:
1: In fitList(p.julian, p.julian.obsvr) :
  Your list was unnamed, so model names were added as object names
2: Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.
3: Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.
4: Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.
> modSel(fitlist)
               nPars    AIC delta AICwt cumltvWt
p.julian.obsvr     8 275.28  0.00  0.72     0.72
p.julian           3 277.16  1.89  0.28     1.00

I know Occu can handle unequal y sample sizes, and that it should remove y observations with no corresponding covariate data (or corresponding NAs). However, that should not be happening with my dataset - all missing y and obsCov values in my data should already have NA values.

I know each obsCov value needs to match a y observation, otherwise both require NAs. Unless I am completely misunderstanding the data structure, I have double-checked to make sure each y NA matches an NA in the appropriate obsCov location. The number of NAs is equal in each variable. My data are in row-major order, with each obsCov variable having a separate column for measurements taken on each survey. Please see the data structure below.

Without understanding why this error is happening, I am hesitant to continue modeling any effects. If anyone sees a reason for the NA error - observation removal, or could make any suggestions that might help me to discover the issue, I would be VERY grateful.

Did you for some reason have a site with y data but no site covariates? Or, is it possible that there was a stray comma or something in your obs covs data that caused the data matrix to have one extra column?

I saw a message regarding a similar warning in an older post to the Unmarked group (Re: Discarded Observations by Kristin Broms on 9/3/10), so I attempted to format my observation covariates in a list so they will be in site-major order. I also manually checked the order of the data using the show(df) function above, and the y, obsCov, and siteCov all appear to line up correctly.



obsCovs <- list(effort=pm.ssoc[,c("effort.1", "effort.2", "effort.3", "effort.4", "effort.5", "effort.6", "effort.7", "effort.8", "effort.9", "effort.10")],

Hey Hardin!

Yes! There was an extra 0 instead of an NA that I didn't see despite STARING at the 698 number several times... Thank you so much, you're my hero!

Best,
Kelsey
On Wednesday, March 14, 2018 at 11:23:42 AM UTC-4, Hardin Waddle wrote:

Kelsey-

You have 698 missing values (NAs) in your y data, but you have 699 in all of the obs covariates. I would check to see if that is right. Did you for some reason have a site with y data but no site covariates? Or, is it possible that there was a stray comma or something in your obs covs data that caused the data matrix to have one extra column?
On Tue, Mar 13, 2018 at 10:41 PM, Kelsey frogsrule Reider <reid...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi,

I'm scared to post on here, especially such a basic question, but I'm stuck on a troublesome formatting issue with my survey covariates in Occu. I swear this should be an easy fix, but I'm not sure what else to try. If anyone would be willing to take a look with me I would sincerely appreciate it.

For the site covariates, my data set has 6 covariates and occu() has no problem
creating models from these:
o.elevation.effort<-occu(~1 ~elevation+avg.effort,pm.ss.std)
> o.elevation.effort

However, when I try to incorporate the survey/observation-specific covariates to model detection, the obsCovs cause R to become unhappy. For example, I get the following errors:


 p.julian<-occu(~julian ~1,pm.ss.std)
Warning message:
Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.

p.julian.obsvr<-occu(~julian+obsvr ~1,pm.ss.std)
Warning message:
Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.

> fitlist<-fitList(p.julian, p.julian.obsvr)
Warning messages:
1: In fitList(p.julian, p.julian.obsvr) :
  Your list was unnamed, so model names were added as object names
2: Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.
3: Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.
4: Some observations have been discarded because corresponding covariates were missing.
> modSel(fitlist)
               nPars    AIC delta AICwt cumltvWt
p.julian.obsvr     8 275.28  0.00  0.72     0.72
p.julian           3 277.16  1.89  0.28     1.00

I know Occu can handle unequal y sample sizes, and that it should remove y observations with no corresponding covariate data (or corresponding NAs). However, that should not be happening with my dataset - all missing y and obsCov values in my data should already have NA values.

I know each obsCov value needs to match a y observation, otherwise both require NAs. Unless I am completely misunderstanding the data structure, I have double-checked to make sure each y NA matches an NA in the appropriate obsCov location. The number of NAs is equal in each variable. My data are in row-major order, with each obsCov variable having a separate column for measurements taken on each survey. Please see the data structure below.

Without understanding why this error is happening, I am hesitant to continue modeling any effects. If anyone sees a reason for the NA error - observation removal, or could make any suggestions that might help me to discover the issue, I would be VERY grateful.
